Subject: Horizon MAP kickoff: performance evaluation & test access

Hi Danielle —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, attaching a concise mutual action plan (MAP) to get the performance evaluation completed and accepted ahead of contract signature. High-level asks here:

- We run a focused benchmark on the production-like test environment (test account + keys we provide).
- Acceptance metrics: median latency & P95 under agreed payload mix, TTFT for cold start <= 150ms, sustained throughput target 800 reqs/min at 16 concurrent clients.
- Scheduling: three load windows (canary, full-run, verification) — propose dates below.

Can you confirm who on your side will own scheduling and whether procurement needs a PO before we hand off test keys? If you prefer, we can stitch the MAP into your DocuSign link.

Proposed quick wins we can deliver in the MAP: technical checklist (test accounts, sample payloads), runbook for load windows, and an artifacts package with raw results + a summary slide for procurement.

I'll loop Rishi and Aditya for logistics and key provisioning.

Thanks,
Monica

Subject: MAP v1 + evaluation plan (payloads, metrics, windows)

Danielle / Markus —

Uploading the MAP v1 here (attached). Summary of key evaluation pieces we will execute as part of the MAP:

1) Test profile & payload mix- 60% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65–256 tokens), 10% long (256–1k tokens).
2) Metrics we capture- Median latency, P95 latency, requests/sec, TTFT (first token time), error rate, CPU/GPU utilization.
3) Concurrency and ramping- Canary: 4 concurrent clients, step 1m ramp to 16c over 10m; Full: target 16–64 concurrent clients with bursts to 96 for 3x 2m windows.
4) Acceptance criteria (for MAP sign-off)- Median latency <= 120ms for short prompts; P95 <= 450ms overall; TTFT cold < 150ms; sustained throughput 750–850 reqs/min.

Logistics notes:
- Environment: redwood-staging-us-west (we will open whitelist for your test CIDRs).
- Test accounts: we will provision two test orgs (hzn-staging-read, hzn-staging-write).
- Keys: ephemeral API keys per load window (see README we attach).
- Artifacts produced: raw token-level traces, aggregated dashboards, and runbook notes.

Proposed load windows (all PST):
- Canary: 2026-04-14 09:00–10:00
- Full run: 2026-04-15 02:00–05:00
- Verification: 2026-04-16 13:00–14:00

If procurement needs to delay keys until contract signature we can still proceed with a limited remote run using a pre-approved LoadForge partner to simulate load; downside is less fidelity on real routing. Let us know preference.

Attached: Horizon_MAP_v1.xlsx (detailed schedule), test_keys_README.txt (key lifecycle & rotation), sample_payloads.json (inline in sheet).

Thanks — looping Rishi for key provisioning and Evelyn to help correlate procurement asks.

Best,
Monica

Subject: MAP results (summary) — Canary + Full-run highlights

Danielle / Markus —

Quick summary of the artifacts produced and results from the MAP activities:

Artifacts delivered:
- hzn_load_results_20260415.json (raw traces)
- Aggregated dashboard (shared link): https://redwood.app/drive/HZN-4583/bench-dashboard
- MAP slide: 1-page summary in Horizon_MAP_v1.xlsx

Key outcomes (Full run via LoadForge simulator; staging environment):
- Short prompts (<=64 tokens): median latency 95ms, P95 310ms.
- Mixed workload overall: median 140ms, P95 480ms.
- TTFT (cold) measured 135ms on average across first-token samples.
- Sustained throughput: sustained 790 reqs/min for 45 minutes; observed burst spikes to 1,100 reqs/min (brief, ~45s) without error-rate increase.
- Concurrency: stable at 32 concurrent workers; transient queueing at 96 bursts (2–3% request queuing).

Notes & next steps:
- The MAP acceptance thresholds in v1 were met for TTFT and short prompt median; P95 was slightly above the 450ms threshold under the heaviest long-prompt mix — we've flagged a suggested kernel tweak and minor batching adjustment. Rishi will open a perf action item for follow-up runs.
- If Horizon wants production-key runs post-PO we recommend a single additional verification run to validate routing and cache warmup on the production network path.

Action items assigned:
- Rishi: bench action item with suggested kernel parameter change and schedule follow-up run (due 2026-04-20).
- Aditya: prepare an invoice-ready summary slide for procurement to attach to the PO (due 2026-04-18).
- Monica: coordinate verification window after PO.

Thanks everyone — overall this gives us a solid baseline for the SOW. I can join procurement calls if it helps accelerate the PO.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
